TLDR and miscellaneous tips at the end

[b]What is it like?[/b]
Cowboy simulator. [u]Smooth animations, a detailed open world, stunning graphics, quality voice acting, and an incredible amount of polish.[/u] When I say this, I speak for both story (Red Dead Redemption 2) and online (Red Dead Online/this product). Both "modes" are actually extremely similar in what you can or cannot do. The main difference is that in online, you get to create and control your own protagonist who experience a different story. Who they become is up to you to decide. The entire map is available for exploration and most, if not all guns/horses/food/etc. available in story are also available in online.

[b]What are the players like?[/b]
[u]What players?[/u] After a few weeks of playing, I can count the number of people I have seen in free roam on my two hands. This can be both good and bad--if you like meeting new people in the game, you're better of using a third party site or platform to find friends. If you like to be immersed or are just weary of griefers, this is a godsend. 
[b]But for the people that I do see, what are they like?[/b] 
GTA Online but most aren't blood-hungry psychopaths or literal Gods. [u]A vast majority of the people you see will probably just ignore you.[/u] Tryhards/griefers and modders/cheaters are present, yes, but they are incredibly rare in my experience.

[b]As for the ingame economy?[/b]
Cash is the standard currency--it's easy to get and earned from most things in the game. Gold is the "premium" currency of Red Dead Online; it can be used to bypass level restrictions, purchase roles, or be used in place of cash. It's a bit harder to come by compared to regular ol' cash, and is rewarded in smaller amounts. You will need a [i]lot[/i] of it. Expect to farm/grind for currency often. Just keep in mind that there's no need to hurry. And don't get burned out. It's also important to note that the way rewards work in this game is a bit weird. In many instances, [u]you get paid MORE cash/gold for taking LONGER to complete a mission or objective. So take your time and enjoy. Don't rush--you'll only sandbag your rewards anyways.[/u]

[b]What should I be doing when I start?[/b]
When you first start out (after the tutorial missions), you will mostly be going to [u]Horley[/u] and doing [u]online's story missions[/u] for early cash and a bit of gold. Once you discover more lucrative sources to make bank, you can sort of "farm the way you want" with [u]specialist roles[/u]. These "roles" or "jobs" let you earn cash by doing specific activities that are exclusive to said role. Like gunplay and lots of action? Save for a bounty hunter pass. Want to start a hunting business? Become a trader. Like alcohol? Sell moonshine! Are you intrigued by animals? Consider becoming a naturalist. Fond of exploration and/or treasure hunting? Collector. Note that getting into roles requires a steep gold investment and that only the bounty hunter role can earn gold from their activities. 

[b]Miscellaneous tips[/b]
 - I recommend you buy the [u]collector bag[/u] to become a collector as soon as possible. With the collector role, you can stock up on treasures found in the open world, then sell them in sets for a large sum of money. Each treasure you collect also gives you experience points to increase your rank. This is especially important because you get a [u]treasure map every 5 ranks[/u] that provides you with a lot of gold and cash in addition to your other sources of income. I recommend looking for antique alcohol bottles and the Swords and Pentacles tarot card sets as these collectible sets are easily obtainable without any additional investment aside from the collector bag, 
- Speaking of collector, hit shift+tab ingame to toggle the Steam overlay. Select "Web Browser" to open a new web browser tab within Steam overlay and search for [u]"jeanropke map".[/u] This will lead you to a site with a virtual Red Dead Online map that updates in real time. With it, you can see the location of every collector item and mark them on your own map ingame. The map also has other important markets for fast travel points, Madam Nazar (collector vendor), legendary animal spawn locations, and some other useful things. 
- Aim to upgrade your Carbine repeater to the [u]Lancaster repeater[/u]. The Lancaster isn't too cheap but it has a high rate of fire as well as balanced range and accuracy, making it an all-around reliable weapon. Oh, and don't forget to [u]clean your weapons[/u] every so often so that their stats are good. To do this, make sure you have gun oil in your inventory (purchased or looted), hover over a weapon and press the scroll wheel/middle click. 
- Press L to pull up the player menu. You can do a lot from here but going to "Online options" at the very bottom allows you to [u]change your playstyle between offensive (on by default) and defensive[/u]. Defensive mode is good for players who aren't looking to pvp, as it gives you damage resistance from players, disables auto aim lock on, immunity from executions and the lasso, and other buffs that promote pacifism. 
- Don't forget to [u]do your daily objectives[/u] (accessible from the player menu, L key). These are actually an incredible source of easy gold. Most challenges are pretty easy and there's always at least a few that don't require pvp or interaction with other players. You only need to complete one daily objective per day to start getting gold reward multipliers for them. The multiplier increases every 7 days, up to 28.
- The game seems to start with very low volume in Window's volume mixer. This is probably because the game's starting cutscene (the shotgun) is actually very loud on max volume. [u]Be sure to check/change the game's volume in Windows mixer every time you boot it up or switch sessions.[/u]

In fact i may have purchased my last game from Rockstar Games over the way we're being treated! Rockstar executives: if you have any sense whatsoever, get a clue, realize you're alienating the very fans who have loyally bought your products for years! You're rewarding player loyalty with a giant figurative middle finger with this latest update, which has caused gameplay to glitch yet again, all because you want to corner us into microtransactions to satisfy your greed! You're already made GTA Online too expensive to bother playing, now you're going to do the same with this game. Just give us story mode DLC. RDR2 Online is not the same as GTA Online. You tried, It failed. The die hard fans still love the original game and want more DLC for single player.

While 5$ may seem like a low price for being able to explore the expansive world of RDR2, there is a reason for that price.

As with GTA 5, Online serves as a money-maker for Rockstar, enabling them to milk the game long after its release.
And sadly time has shown Rockstar to be quite the greedy company, despite their excellent and good-selling singleplayer games. These greedy tendencies show themselves in Red Dead Online as well: What you are paying for here is practically a (near)free to play, microtransaction laden experience full of grind.

Around every corner the game incentivizes the purchase of "gold bars", which are the premium currency. These gold bars can also be earned in-game at a slow, excruciating pace, through missions and daily challenges. 
One of the main features of Online, namely the "Professions", are locked behind the gold bar currency. Unlocking only one of the five currently available professions will set you back 15 gold bars, which can take several days to acquire.

Speaking of features, there are a lot things that are missing from Online, like being able to steal/tame wild horses and keep them (or at least sell them), bank heists, small wilderness camps, the ability to take a bath, and many more. A lot of these features are present in singleplayer, and would not be hard to implement.
And while new content is being added to the game regularly, the quality of that content seems to be declining with time. Bugs are not uncommon, and some easy-to-fix ones persist through multiple updates.
It really is a shame that Rockstar are taking the game down such a path, as there is potential for a lot of fun content.

At the end of the day, the core gameplay can still be enjoyable, especially with some friends. But i cannot recommend a game with such terrible business practices.

- Friends play game, suggest buying it

- cowboy shenanigans ensue
- next week, no one playing once again
- "too big of a game to keep on hard drive"
- uninstall, and put back on the shelf for next years fleeting interest from friends

Rinse and Repeat as needed for best results.

There are quite a few positives to Red Dead Online. I played it on PS4 for quite a while before buying it here and had an okay time. It was a fun way to spend a few hours.  

A few positives: 
- You get to play Red Dead with your friends
- Taking screenshots in this game is a lot of fun
- Exploring the world with your friends is great! 
- There's lots of opportunity for customisation

However,
The whole point of this game is to waste the player's time or take their money. It takes so long to get the in-game currency and I strongly believe that if you took the grinding elements out of this game there would be nothing left of it. There's barely anything to do in this game besides grind for gold and do PVP.  

The roles in this game are kind of silly. You pay a bunch of gold to get access to key game-play elements that shouldn't be behind essentially what is a paywall. Without them you can only do a few things and even when you do get them, they barely have any substance and get stale after doing missions the first few times. It'll take you at least 10-15 hours of game time to grind the boring stranger missions to get enough gold to buy the bounty hunter licence. And then another 10 hours to grind enough to get one of the others and it's just an endless cycle of wasting time so you can do basic things. Then finally once you've unlocked everything, what is there to do? You don't get anything for any of these roles other than extra money making opportunities. All that grinding is literally for nothing.  

The only time this game is fun is when you're playing it with others. 

Though,
It gets incredibly annoying when you and your friends are trying to have a nice chill time, doing some fishing or doing a few missions, and a posse of people start harassing you and blowing you up just because they can. Sure, you can move lobbies, but the fact that you can't make a private lobby for just you and your friends is stupid. I know they could add it if they wanted to, they have it in GTA, but Rockstar are lazy. 

They won't even ban hackers. Hackers are a whole other issue that you should look into when considering to get this game as the game still uses P2P connections instead of actual servers. (this way Rockstar gets to save money at the expense of the user's safety.) Hackers can easily get your IP address. Always use a VPN when playing this game or GTA Online. 
There have been cases where unsuspecting players open chests they find on the ground that are spawned in by hackers (these give you gold and money) and then they proceeded to ban the unsuspecting player. Rockstar won't do anything about said hackers but will ban innocent players.

Overall I like this game, and will probably continue to play it, but I will not give Rockstar any more of my money until they get their crap together. As long as they get money for doing the least amount of work possible, they'll continue. This is why I urge you not to keep paying them (like I stupidly did) until they actually try, or show that they care about their community.

"Have you ever heard the tragedy of Red Dead Online?"
"No."
"I thought not. It's not a tale the cowboys would tell you. It's a gamer legend. It had such attention to detail, players could even form posses and go bounty hunting."

"They could actually... create their own story?"
"The open world of Red Dead Online is a gateway to many experiences... some consider to be extraordinary."
"Wh– What happened to it?"

"Did that... ruin the game?"
"Over time, it did. As the developers became more focused on their greed for money, they neglected the essential aspects of the game and its community. Players began to lose interest, feeling that the game was becoming more of a cash grab than an immersive Wild West experience. The once thriving community started to dwindle, leaving behind a shell of what was once a remarkable game."

"Is there any hope for Red Dead Online?"

Let me start off with, I love this game. This is probably a shock considering I gave it a thumbs down. The sights are beautiful and really hammers home the wild west themes. In general, the game is fun to play. Mechanics and story are great, loads of character customization, and a wonderful general feel of living out in the west. There are a few things I'd wish to be added but they don't detract from the game. Such as being able to lay down at your campsite for maybe increased healing or aesthetic. Selling stolen horses or captured horses since that is literally the tutorial but something not implemented in the online. But these things don't break the game. Don't make me not want to play it. Just things that would be cool to have.

What does break the game is hacking. While this is not Red Dead exclusive, and certainly not Rockstar exclusive, Rockstar has a habit of having little to no anti-cheat matched with little to no care about such hackers. It's only gotten worse over the years. People randomly killing you (not from the PvP) with different methods such as spawning a bear while you're in your safe zone so you are either killed by the bear(s) or insta-killed by the hacker once leaving the safe zone. A general  random teleport that could be a simple prank to lets throw you off a cliff multiple times, and to finally stealing your money. I've had all three happen to me. The last one relatively new to me but that I've now decided enough was enough. The other ones, annoying. Just moved to a different session. This last one, the last straw. 

You may think, well just earn your money up again. Unfortunately it's not quite so easy. The cash sure. Was super frustrating, but the gold bars and tokens are much harder. Gold bars can be earned by earning little nuggets. So it isn't even a full gold bar. It's like gather a whole bunch of cents to try and make a dollar. Sometimes you find a quarter, but most of the time it's nickels or pennies. So of course, it is typically a pay for currency. Using real money to buy the gold bars. That's a problem if someone keeps stealing it. At that point, they might as well be stealing real money. And finally tokens, only given when you level up in your job. That means they are finite. Unless you can earn more after maxing out your jobs not entirely sure. Haven't gotten there yet, because hackers keep me from enjoying this game.

And that sums up my review. The reason I don't recommend getting it, is simply because of hackers. And more importantly, hackers being allowed to get away with their hacking.

First, there are hackers. They can basically do what they want when they want. Most commonly, you'll be shot with explosive ammo and killed in a very acrobatic fashion. More rarely, they will not kill you and will mess with you. I've been harassed in so many ways it's just mind numbing. I lose time and in game cash. That is annoying. Not everyone is hacker, but you will encounter them. They likely come from one country in particular. However, there is simply no way to play on servers that exclude those countries. You just have to grin and bear the brunt of their foolishness. It's probably baked into the contract that Rockstar has with that country they can't be blocked from servers. I'm far from an expert and I'm disgruntled as a user. Take my opinions with a grain of salt. Also, there is no way to report a hacker that is reliable. To be fair, I paid $10 for this game and purchased $20 worth of in game gold. Have I received my $30 worth in game? Probably. Am I a happy customer? Not really.

If they would simply find a way to stop the hackers or allow us to propagate semi-private lobbies, this would be ideal. That's easy for me to say, right? As others have said, the griefers and modders make the game basically unplayable in [I]public[/I] lobbies. You will be teleported away from what ever you were doing at random times, killed repeatedly by people you can't even see, and be subjected to immersion breaking things like UFO's, unnaturally large creatures, and weirdly sized or colored players. However, if you learn how to do a private lobby using a text file, the game is glorious! I play this way with a friend, and while I miss the interaction with other decent people (they exist!), I  never have to worry about random disconnects or being griefed while I enjoy the stunning landscapes and just going about my business in the game world. My favorite parts of the game are the horses, clothing options, and realism of the game world. The PC UI takes some getting used to, and I could do without a lot of the forced grouping and combat, but otherwise this has become my favorite game. The horses are the best game horses I've ever seen and interacted with, and it's a pleasure to just ride slowly down the roads and trails and enjoy the wildlife and scenery. 

Tips: It's worth it to buy enough gold to get the Collector Role as soon as you can. This Role will easily give you the ingame cash you need to maintain your camp, pay for stables, and keep your horse well fed while you get going. Do the dailies and treasure maps (you get one every 5 levels) to make the gold to purchase your next Role. Loot all the NPC's you kill - they don't have much cash, but sometimes you will get a treasure map, things you can sell to a Fence, gun oil, and other useful items.
